FROMLIST: devfreq: add mediatek cci devfreq This adds a devfreq driver for the Cache Coherent Interconnect (CCI) of the Mediatek MT8183. On the MT8183 the CCI is supplied by the same regulator as the LITTLE cores. The driver is notified when the regulator voltage changes (driven by cpufreq) and adjusts the CCI frequency to the maximum possible value. (am from https://patchwork.kernel.org/patch/10946063/) BUG=b:129039370 TEST=boot to shell Change-Id: I1f62d27e16406a555fae2d69f4a9e0436cd4b3ed Signed-off-by: Andrew-sh.Cheng <andrew-sh.cheng@mediatek.com> Signed-off-by: Eddie Huang <eddie.huang@mediatek.com> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1631077 Commit-Ready: Nicolas Boichat <drinkcat@chromium.org> Tested-by: Nicolas Boichat <drinkcat@chromium.org> Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Nicolas Boichat <drinkcat@chromium.org>

FROMLIST: PM / OPP: Support adjusting OPP voltages at runtime On some SoCs the Adaptive Voltage Scaling (AVS) technique is employed to optimize the operating voltage of a device. At a given frequency, the hardware monitors dynamic factors and either makes a suggestion for how much to adjust a voltage for the current frequency, or it automatically adjusts the voltage without software intervention. Add an API to the OPP library for the former case, so that AVS type devices can update the voltages for an OPP when the hardware determines the voltage should change. The assumption is that drivers like CPUfreq or devfreq will register for the OPP notifiers and adjust the voltage according to suggestions that AVS makes. This patch is devired from [1] submitted by Stephen. [1] https://lore.kernel.org/patchwork/patch/599279/ (am from https://patchwork.kernel.org/patch/10946069/) BUG=b:129039370 TEST=boot to shell Change-Id: I1bc83a75bb0577a084c40411829fca19af8b0b58 Signed-off-by: Stephen Boyd <sboyd@codeaurora.org> Signed-off-by: Roger Lu <roger.lu@mediatek.com> Signed-off-by: Eddie Huang <eddie.huang@mediatek.com> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1628412 Commit-Ready: Nicolas Boichat <drinkcat@chromium.org> Tested-by: Nicolas Boichat <drinkcat@chromium.org> Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Nicolas Boichat <drinkcat@chromium.org>

crash: Use zlib instead of invoking gzip For file compression in crash_reporter and crash_sender, integrate zlib and use zlib C++ functions instead of invoking the gzip program as a separate process. This is simpler (no file descriptor polling code), and faster and more reliable (no separate process to fork and exec and check error returns). It also is necessary to make UploadSingleCrash work (see chromium:857317). I need control of the file descriptor that the compressed data is being written to, so that I can capture it for the UploadSingleCrash D-Bus message. BUG=chromium:857317 TEST=Uploaded crashes from user programs, kernel_wifi_warning, chrome, service failure, and udev. Ensured that crashes appeared on crash-staging and that the log files were valid gzip files (could be downloaded and gunzip'ed). cros-kernel2.eclass: Add support for device tree compression This patch adds support for the new device tree compression feature for which firmware support was added to depthcharge in CL:1553458. Compressed device trees shrink to less than a third of the size and thus reduce the overall size of the FIT image, increasing boot speed. This feature is supposed to be the new default for all future Chrome OS devices, so this patch enables it by default to make sure we don't have to carry a special USE flag forever and risk forgetting it every time we add a new board. However, since the feature requires firmware support, it needs to be explicitly disabled on all previously shipped boards (see dependent CLs). The only board families that will have it enabled to start with are Cheza, Kukui and Mistral. BUG=None TEST=Built and booted Kevin, confirmed that FDTs were still uncompressed. Built and booted Kevin with explicit USE=dt_compression, confirmed that FDTs were compressed and that ToT depthcharge could boot them correctly. Cq-Depend: chromium:1621519,chrome-internal:1323952,chrome-internal:1324624,chrome-internal:1323953,chrome-internal:1324499,chrome-internal:1320522 Change-Id: I7651b9b87d91e14e5baa8872f7e6cc444c186bf9 Signed-off-by: Julius Werner <jwerner@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1621487 Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org>
